scope: separate finite synthetic methods benchmark; no source data, no new EOG-WF endpoint; 3/31/3 unchanged

generator.algorithm: same v4 generator, new seed: Python random.Random; draw env randint(0,3) for each lexicographic time/site state; loop lexicographic ordered vertex pairs; if 1<=dt<=2 and rng.random()<0.40, draw barrier randint(0,2) then hard rng.random()<0.10; keep iff not hard, abs(site difference)<=2*dt, abs(env difference)<=2, barrier<=1. Explicit waiting only.

damage: all 16 damage masks D on four candidate sites; restore any R subset D; original edges restored exactly when both endpoints available; no other change; source and targets protected

estimands.local: inclusion-minimal R giving reachability in each fixed world
estimands.possible: inclusion-minimal R giving reachability in at least one complete world
estimands.robust: inclusion-minimal R giving reachability in every complete world (paths may differ)
estimands.status: already reachable => {empty restoration}; infeasible even intact => empty family; exclude already reachable from repair-needed counts
estimands.duality: for each D and each monotone predicate F (world-local, possible or robust), define mathematical cut family C_D=min{K subset D: F(intact minus K)=false}; min repair family = minimal hitting sets of C_D; C_D={empty set} is algebraic marker of intact infeasibility, not an actionable destructive cut; C_D=empty family means no allowed cut
estimands.aggregation: possible=minimal union of local repair families; robust=minimal unions of one repair from each local family, infeasible if any empty. No cross-world edge splicing.
estimands.primary: for D=all four sites, count minimum destruction vs restoration sizes for possible and robust predicates only when intact true, damaged false; classify restoration size greater/equal/less; report joint distribution, plus robust restoration size > possible in same eligible systems and no common singleton when each world has singleton repair
estimands.secondary: all damage masks: compare direct reachability to independently enumerated path signatures, compare restoration families with oracle and cut duality, aggregate identities; retain denominators and empty/already-satisfied statuses

canonical.serial: one world path 00->11->23->45, two removable sites {1,3}; min cut size 1, min repair 2 from all-disabled
canonical.parallel: one world, target40: paths 00->11->20->40 and 00->12->20->40; signatures {1},{2}; min cut 2, repair 1
canonical.world_disagreement: target40, separate singleton paths via sites 1 and 2 in two worlds, third duplicates first; possible repair singleton, robust repair pair; all-world loss pair, robust loss singleton
canonical.uncuttable_and_infeasible: explicit source-site path 00->20->40 always reachable; empty-edge world impossible; verify both algebraic empty boundaries

oracle: per world enumerate all source-target paths via DFS, store visited-site masks; for each mask direct forward reachability must agree with path signature oracle; for every D compare direct minimal restoration families against minimal path requirements (world), union/combinations thereof (aggregate), and minimal hitting sets of cut family; verify monotonicity and exact boundary statuses
success: zero oracle/duality/aggregation/monotonicity mismatches; canonical witnesses pass; no expected direction or prevalence threshold
stop: conditional restoration of same frozen edges only; no regeneration, demographic recovery or conservation efficacy claim; no new source access, no production API, no main merge.
pre_score_clarification: Remove extraneous discarded parallel-path text; final target40 paths unchanged, no scoring performed. All generator and estimands unchanged.
